question: After the no-op pacing bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept pending recoverable ambiguous outbound rows as this interim delivery-consistency mitigation?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes existing upgrade/runtime behavior for ambiguous queued sends, and automation can fix the pacing bug but cannot decide the product tradeoff between recoverability, operator visibility, and terminal failure semantics.

options.title: Accept after pacing fix
options.body: Land the mitigation after unavailable-reconciler rows no longer consume replay pacing, leaving the broader delivery ledger and UI/API surfacing to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87544.

options.title: Require broader design first
options.body: Hold this PR until the delivery ledger, reconciler semantics, and operator-visible states are designed together.

options.title: Close as too narrow
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers prefer not to change queue terminal-state behavior without the broader reconciliation surface.

recommendation.title: Accept after pacing fix
recommendation.body: Land the mitigation after unavailable-reconciler rows no longer consume replay pacing, leaving the broader delivery ledger and UI/API surfacing to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87544.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows steipete authored or merged the closest outbound recovery changes and is the best available owner for the tradeoff.
